maria: Quick RFC follow-up on the kernel selector for GQA vs MQA. We need a minimal runtime contract: selection, capabilities, and explicit KV cache rules. Kicking off a short thread before the sync.

kevin: @maria +1. My high-level: selector should be a pure function of model_spec + request_shape + cost_hint. Output a KernelDescriptor (name, capability bits, batching strategy). Keep it stateless for easier testing.

jordan: Major concern = KV cache semantics. Grouped-query expects shared KV prefixes between grouped items; MQA multiplexes KV per query. Interface must make cache scope explicit so we never leak one request's cache into another.

lisa: Quick proposal for selector signature:
```
select_kernel({
  model_id,
  seq_len,
  batch_size_hint,
  latency_slo_ms,
  cost_pref: 'cheap'|'balanced'|'fast'
}) -> {
  kernel_name,
  capabilities: ['gqa','mqa','prefetch'],
  cache_scope: 'per-request'|'per-session'|'per-kernel-instance'
}
```
Then runtime uses kernel.run(batch, cache_handle). Keep cache_handle explicit.

sam: Also add telemetry tags at decision time: kernel=..., decision_reason=..., est_token_cost, expected_p99. Makes rollbacks and cost debugging much easier.

kevin: Fallback semantics? If a kernel fails mid-run, should we retry on another kernel variant? I think yes, but we need idempotency guarantees and a cheap probe mode so we don't amplify latency. Maybe return a special error that runtime interprets as retryable.

maria: Agreed. Fallback policy suggestion: primary -> quick health probe -> fallback kernel of same model family -> if fallback used emit regression alert and sample payloads. Use a requeue path to avoid head-of-line blocking for the batch.

jordan: Who owns kernel lifecycle: runtime or model loader? I vote model loader owns compiled kernels and artifacts; runtime keeps references and decides instantiation/warmup. That keeps compile/prepare concerns out of the hot path.

lisa: Note on warmup: MQA kernels benefit from pre-populated KV structures and prefetch hooks. Add warmup callback in the kernel interface: kernel.warmup(seed_prompts) that returns an estimated_ready_score.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary:kernel-selector-v2 deployed to eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-20T10:12:00Z :rocket:

sam: Action items: 1) @kevin draft PR with selector interface and validation tests, 2) @jordan define KV cache scope unit/integration tests and invariants, 3) @lisa add telemetry + tracing fields to selector decisions, 4) @maria schedule 30m sync to lock tradeoffs. I'll write short RFC addendum.

maria: Thanks — I'll also add a test matrix (seq_len x batch x cost_pref) and a short checklist for regression alerts. Sync scheduled: 2026-03-21 14:00 PT. :thumbsup:
